solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; clues and answers read from cryptics.georgeho.org (ODbL)'s copy of the post, which drops the counts, so each count is read off the blogger's answer

clue.text: Something precious from old friend

blocks.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: A treasured keepsake handed down by a long-time friend.
explanation.definitionFit: This milky iridescent stone is a gem, valued as jewellery, so it counts as a precious thing.

clue.text: With mobile phone I’ll get by in desert city

indicators.note: mobile means able to move about, so the letters of the next word are moved into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written before rearranging
taken as written, from I'll
by as in multiplication, two by three, written with the times sign X

explanation.surface: Someone lost in the desert reckons a mobile phone will see them through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mobile phone' reads as one object, but mobile is the signal that reshuffles phone; 'get by' splits, with by becoming the multiplication X.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arizona state capital sits in the Sonoran Desert, so it is a city in arid country.

clue.text: Spill pickle? More flimsy sandwiches

indicators.note: to sandwich something is to hold it between two layers, so one word encloses the other

blocks.note: a lame excuse is a flimsy one, so more flimsy is lamer
to be in a pickle is to be in a fix, a plight

explanation.surface: A spilt jar of pickle trapped in a feeble sandwich.
explanation.walkthrough: Spill here is not an accident but a noun: a thin strip of wood or paper used to light a fire or lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamplighter is a taper or spill used for lighting lamps, as well as the person who lit street lamps.

clue.text: Undermine reason to keep current literature

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside, so the first word holds the following pieces

blocks.note: to reason with someone is to argue, to debate
I is the physics symbol for electric current
lit is the common short form of literature

explanation.surface: An argument meant to protect live electrical writing ends up weakening it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reason' looks like a noun meaning cause; here it is the verb meaning to argue a point.
explanation.definitionFit: To debilitate is to weaken or sap strength, which is what undermining someone or something does.

clue.text: Perversely I had fling, being attractive

indicators.note: perversely means turned the wrong way, so the contracted words are read backwards

blocks.note: I had contracts to I'd
to shy a ball is to fling it, as at a coconut shy

explanation.surface: A confession of a wayward affair with someone good-looking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fling' suggests an affair; here it is the verb to throw. Dishy is British slang for good-looking.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishy is informal British slang for good-looking, used of a person one fancies.

clue.text: Number he sings in funny duo’s closing piece

indicators.note: funny means odd or peculiar, so the words before it are jumbled into a strange new order

blocks.note: all fifteen letters are taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: A song performed by a comic double act at the end of their show.
explanation.walkthrough: The duo is Morecambe and Wise, the much-loved British comedy pair whose TV shows ended with them dancing off to this song. 'Funny' fits the comedy surface but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Morecambe and Wise used this song as the signature tune that closed every television show they made.

clue.text: House with shed in road on river

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other, the shed sitting within the road

blocks.note: a lane is a narrow road
a snake's cast skin is shed, so shed means cast
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A property with an outbuilding on a road beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House' and 'shed' suggest buildings; shed is the verb meaning cast off, and House is a royal dynasty.
explanation.definitionFit: The royal House of Lancaster was the English dynasty of Henry IV, V and VI in the Wars of the Roses.

clue.text: Japanese fish that is regularly seen

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so only every other letter of the phrase is kept

blocks.note: the first, third and fifth letters of the phrase

explanation.surface: A remark on a fish often spotted in Japanese waters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tai is the Japanese red sea bream, a prized fish served at celebrations in Japan.

clue.text: Couple carrying tiny new child

indicators.note: carrying means holding something within, so the first word holds the next pieces

blocks.note: to couple things is to tie them together
wee is Scottish and British informal for tiny
N is the standard abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Two parents carrying their very small newborn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Couple' looks like a pair of people; it is the verb meaning to join. TIE holds WEE and N.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweenie is a youngster between infancy and teenage years, roughly eight to twelve, so a kind of child.

clue.text: Doorman’s voice after calling in advance

indicators.note: after means coming later, so the word before it is written second, behind the following phrase

blocks.note: a commission is a task or post one is called to, ordered and agreed beforehand
an air is a melody for the voice; AIRE is the French spelling this borrowed word keeps

explanation.surface: A hotel doorman phones ahead to announce guests.
explanation.definitionFit: A commissionaire is a uniformed attendant at the entrance of a hotel, cinema or office building.

clue.text: Person initially into dental work out of touch?

definitions.note: the question mark flags a definition by negation: not out of touch

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of the word is used
into means going inside, so that letter is placed within the next piece

blocks.note: the first letter of the word
an inlay is a filling fitted into a tooth

explanation.surface: A dentist so absorbed in work they are oblivious to the world.
explanation.walkthrough: Touch is the area outside the sidelines in rugby and football; a ball out of touch is back in the field of play. The definition answers the question with a phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: In ball games a ball not over the touchline is live, still counted as part of the game.

clue.text: Mercenary run, a run to intercept goods

indicators.note: to intercept is to come between, so the pieces sit in the middle of the last word

blocks.note: G is short for good, so goods doubles it
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
taken as written
a spin is a short drive or run out in a car

explanation.surface: A hired soldier making a dash to seize a shipment of supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: The same word run gives two different pieces. R, A and SPIN sit between the two Gs.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone greedy and money-minded, interested chiefly in personal gain.

clue.text: Walk for a mile through exotic tableau

indicators.note: through means passing into the middle, so the letter goes inside the following word
exotic means strange and foreign, so the letters are turned into an unfamiliar order

blocks.note: per means for each, as in ten pounds per head
M is the abbreviation for mile
taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: A tourist strolling a mile across a foreign scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For a' together give PER, then M joins the letters of tableau and all are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To perambulate is a formal verb for walking about or strolling, especially around a place.

clue.text: IO2U?

blocks.note: surface reading: a string of letters and a digit like a code or chemical formula
setter's reading: the familiar IOU note with the formula for the breathing gas written inside it

explanation.walkthrough: IOU is the written promise to pay back money, a debt. Putting O2 inside it reads as I owe O2 to you, a debt of the gas.
explanation.definitionFit: The physiological term names the shortfall of the breathing gas the body builds up during hard exercise and repays afterwards by panting.

clue.text: When metal is found in loch, is this pollution?

definitions.note: loose: nastiness as foulness or unpleasantness

indicators.note: to be found in something is to be located inside it, so the pieces sit within the loch

blocks.note: Loch Ness, the famous Scottish lake
as means when, as in as I left
tin is a metal

explanation.surface: Asking whether metal discovered in a Scottish lake amounts to contamination.
explanation.walkthrough: Loch Ness is the famous Scottish lake, so loch alone can stand for its name.
explanation.definitionFit: Nastiness means foulness or filthiness, the unpleasant quality that dirty, contaminated water has.

clue.text: Hum — create sounds like this

indicators.note: sounds like says the answer is pronounced the same as the word before it

blocks.note: to wreak havoc is to create it; the two spellings are said alike

explanation.surface: A singer is told to make a humming noise in imitation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hum' looks like a musical sound, but in British slang a hum is a bad smell.
explanation.definitionFit: In informal British usage a hum is an unpleasant odour, and a reek is a strong bad smell.

clue.text: Alien is on the way — leave it!

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the first piece follows the second when written out

blocks.note: St is short for street, a way
ET is the film alien

explanation.surface: A warning that an alien is coming, so hands off.
explanation.walkthrough: Stet is the proofreader's Latin instruction meaning let it stand, cancelling a correction.
explanation.definitionFit: Editors write this Latin word, meaning let it stand, beside a marked passage to cancel a correction.

clue.text: Shudder as male breaks into soprano

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it, so one letter enters the voice part

blocks.note: a treble is a high voice, a boy soprano
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A man's interruption of a soprano's aria makes the audience wince.
explanation.walkthrough: M goes inside TREBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean to quiver or shake involuntarily, from fear, cold or excitement.

clue.text: Wanting equaliser, puts away header for Man City

indicators.note: wanting means deficient or not right, so the word that follows is reordered
to put away food is to take it inside, so the word swallows the next letter
a header is the top or start, so only the opening letter of the next word is used

blocks.note: taken as written before rearranging
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A football report: a side chasing a late leveller heads one in for Manchester City.
explanation.walkthrough: The football surface makes Man City look like the team; City alone is the definition. The Square Mile is the City of London, its financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: The historic City of London covers roughly one square mile, giving the financial district its nickname.

clue.text: Almost lay beneath trough

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the next word loses its final letter

blocks.note: taken as written before trimming
under means beneath

explanation.surface: Something lay nearly underneath a feeding trough.
explanation.walkthrough: The word usually means to wash or to clean dirty money; here it is the rarer noun, a channel for water used in mining.
explanation.definitionFit: A launder is a channel or gutter carrying water, used especially in mining to wash ore.

clue.text: Pawn most of first teeth

indicators.note: most of means nearly all, so the last letter of the next word is dropped

blocks.note: P is the chess notation for pawn
the first is the earliest

explanation.surface: Pawning nearly all of a child's milk teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: Pawn looks like a verb about hocking goods; it is the chess piece. Pearlies is informal for teeth, from their white shine.
explanation.definitionFit: Pearly whites, shortened to pearlies, is a jokey informal name for a person's set of teeth.

clue.text: Can it eat when cabin opens?

indicators.note: the cabin opens the other word by splitting it apart and sitting in the gap

blocks.note: to sup is to eat supper
a hut is a small cabin

explanation.surface: Asking whether food can be eaten when the cafe in the cabin opens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can it' looks like a question; it is slang for stop talking.
explanation.definitionFit: Can it is a slang command to be quiet, the same rude instruction as telling someone to stop talking.

clue.text: Shoe to briefly knock up

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the next word loses its last letter
in a down clue up means read from bottom to top, backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
to bash is to knock or strike

explanation.surface: A cobbler is asked to knock a shoe together quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knock up' looks like a phrase meaning make quickly; up is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A sabot is a wooden clog, the heavy carved footwear worn by French and Dutch peasants.

clue.text: Notice places where slugs hide in food

indicators.note: to hide something is to keep it inside and out of sight, so the first word encloses the rest

blocks.note: slugs are bullets
taken as written
board is food, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: Signs warning of spots where garden slugs lurk in the vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slugs' suggests garden pests; they are bullets, and board is food as in bed and board.
explanation.definitionFit: These are boards where announcements and notices are pinned up for people to read.

clue.text: Lions, but not on heraldic device

indicators.note: but not means without, so the following word is removed from the first

blocks.note: taken as written before removal
taken as written; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: A coat of arms showing lions but without the usual symbol.
explanation.walkthrough: Lions are common heraldic beasts, which makes the surface convincing.
explanation.definitionFit: A lis is the fleur-de-lis, the stylised lily emblem used as a charge in coats of arms.

clue.text: Prolonged parking worked in streets

indicators.note: worked means shaped or kneaded, so the letters that follow are reworked into a new order

blocks.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: Long-term parking operated on city roads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worked' fits the parking surface but signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Something persistent continues or lasts for a long time, as a lingering cough does.

clue.text: Make a spike point

blocks.note: an ear of corn is its spike of grain
N, north, is a compass point

explanation.surface: An instruction to sharpen something to a tip.
explanation.walkthrough: Spike here is botanical, the head of a cereal plant.
explanation.definitionFit: To make money is to gain it as income, the everyday sense of being paid for work.
